sky.teaching: the cardinal air of the scales, weighing each thing against another to find where balance falls. Justice's sky, the season that holds day and night in equal measure before the year tips toward dark.

immortals.teaching: Lu Dong Bin stands above, the scholar-swordsman whose blade cuts through delusion and ignorance, and He Xian Gu below, the one woman among the immortals, who ate the powder of stone and lives on purity and breath. Nothing is refined by the blade alone. The cut sorts true from false, and a purity fed on stone dust and breath supplies the slow heat that finishes the work.

hebrew_letter.teaching: the goad that guides the ox with a steady prod, the gentle correction that keeps a thing moving toward its right path. The patient steering of the one who tunes and re-tunes until the rasp becomes a note.

cards.essence: Shock is this energy: the sudden thing you did not choose, and the part of you that moves first when it comes. It is the jolt that wakes what was sleeping, in the ground as in you, and it comes without warning because that is what a jolt is. In a life it is the one who goes first, off the edge of what anyone has done, and the one the unexpected finds more often than most. You carry more charge than the people around you. It will not let you sit still, and it was never meant to.

glance.reading:
Shock is this energy: the sudden thing you did not choose, and the part of you that moves first when it comes. It is the jolt that wakes what was sleeping, in the ground as in you, and it comes without warning because that is what a jolt is. In a life it is the one who goes first, off the edge of what anyone has done, and the one the unexpected finds more often than most. You carry more charge than the people around you. It will not let you sit still, and it was never meant to.

Shock runs on a trust that is in the body or nowhere, once you lean into it. Trusting life is not a thought you have or a mood you work up; your cells have it or they do not, and everything else follows from that. With it, the charge in you becomes the nerve to move. You take the step, and the taking of it is what changes things, inside first, outside after. The more you believe in yourself and act on it, the more life comes to meet you; it will surprise you with good fortune. The ones who go first are not leaders. They are the ones who show there was a path.

The way through is softness. What shakes you cannot be braced against, because bracing is how a shock breaks a person; leaned into rather than fought, the same blow passes through and leaves you standing somewhere new. Every shock is a door, if you are pliant enough to go through it. It breaks a hole in the walls you took for the world, and lets you out of a safety that was never real. Soften, let it in, and take the step it was pushing you toward.

iching.trigram_combination: Thunder over Thunder: the same shock twice, the second peal breaking before the first has died away, out of a power that rises from deep in the ground. The traditional character sets rain falling from a cloud over a sign that once meant the shock, and in the old calendar that sign named the day the first thunder wakes whatever slept the winter.
iching.reading:
Something has struck without warning, and it has changed the shape of the day. It comes with its own sound: the cry when it lands, then the laughing, because the blow passed and you are still here. Everyone within a hundred miles heard it. What they do with it is the question, and most people jump, then forget, then go back to talking, having learned nothing.

What this asks of you is to be the one whose hand does not shake. The old picture is a person in the temple holding the ladle of wine when the thunder breaks overhead, and not a drop is spilled, because they were so far inside their work that the noise could not reach the hand. You cannot choose what strikes. You can choose your reply: stay at the centre of it, where a storm is calm, and go on with what is yours to do. Fear is the warning, and the care it makes in you is where the luck comes from; let it make you careful, then let it go. Use the shaking to look at your life, and set in order what it shows. What you lost comes back in time, or turns out not to have been needed.

In the body this energy is the feet. Notice where you are holding yourself now: up on your toes, ready to run, or rooted so hard you cannot move. Put your weight down through both feet and feel the ground, still there. Steady the feet, and the hand steadies with them.
judgement_lines: Shock comes, and it brings you through. Alarm first, then laughing words.
It frightens a hundred miles, and the ladle of wine is not spilled.
image_lines: Thunder repeated, one peal on another: the picture of shock.
So the wise, in fear and trembling, set their life in order, then look at themselves.

upper_trigram.name: Thunder (Chen)
upper_trigram.nature: Arousing power emerging from the depth of the earth. Excite, influence, move, affect. The eldest son.

lower_trigram.name: Thunder (Chen)
lower_trigram.nature: Arousing power emerging from the depth of the earth. Excite, influence, move, affect. The eldest son.

lines.image: the shock comes, alarm, then laughing.
lines.reading: The first peal lands and you jump, looking round to see what it was. Then it passes, smaller than the fright of it, and the fright comes out of you as laughter. That order is the right one: wary first, glad after. Be alert when it comes, because what you learn in the fright is the rule you live by afterwards.

lines.image: treasures lost, the nine hills climbed, and back in seven days.
lines.reading: The shock comes with real loss, and what you valued is scattered. Every part of you wants to go down into the wreck after it. Do not. Climb instead, up to where you can see the whole of it, and let the loss be a loss for now. What was yours comes back in seven days, once the cycle has turned, and you were not chasing it.

lines.image: distraught in the shock, and moved to act by it.
lines.reading: The shaking has left you unable to think, and the sound is already fainter than it was. That is its own danger, because a fright that is fading lets you go slack. Let even the faint sound move you. If you cannot find the strength in yourself, borrow it from someone who has it. Moved to act, you come to no harm.

lines.image: thunder sunk in the mud.
lines.reading: The shock lands in soft ground and is swallowed; nothing comes of it. There was force in it, with no firm footing under the force, so it went nowhere and its light never showed. This is the blow that should have moved you and left you sunk instead. Feel where the ground gave, and begin again from the bottom.

lines.image: the shock going and coming, and business still to do.
lines.reading: The shock comes, goes, comes again, so there is danger on the way out and danger on the way back. Hold the middle of yourself through it. Nothing that matters is lost here, whatever it looks like from inside the noise. There is work in front of you that has not gone away. Stay balanced, act carefully, and do what must be done.

lines.image: shock at the top, eyes darting, and the strike landing next door.
lines.reading: At the far end of the shaking the strength has gone and only the fear is left, the eyes darting, the body unable to move. Set out from here and it goes badly. The blow has not reached you yet; it has reached your neighbour, and that is the warning. Take it while it is still next door, whatever the family says. Be the one who does not shake.

gene_keys.shadow:
At any moment something could happen to you, and you know it. The people you love, the next hour: none of it is promised, and most of the time the knowing sits behind a door. Agitation is what leaks under it, a hum of fear that does not stop. You watch a blow land on someone else, in the next street, and your body files it: this house could be next. There is a great deal of charge in that state, and it cannot sit still; it looks for a reaction, any reaction, doing reckless things for the release. Run at life or flinch from it: either way the fear is untouched. It learns to compete, needing to be first not to grow but to feel above the others, and that is a way of not looking at death, which humbles everyone at the top.

Trust is not a thought or a mood; it is in your body or it is not, and the agitation is the sound a body makes without it. Pushed down, it shuts you; thrown out, it hurts whoever is nearest. Nothing on the outside will settle it, since nothing on the outside started it.
gene_keys.repressive: Fear has been left to rule this person, though they could walk out of it. They lost hope a little at a time, turned inward and shut down, until nothing much interests them. The real fear is of facing the fear; faced, it turns out to be nothing. Only they can do that.
gene_keys.reactive: The other kind throws it outward. A fearless rage sits over a deep sense that nothing matters, and it goes looking for the edge: the dangerous job, the fight nobody asked for, shocking people for no reason. It passes for courage and is only fear shouted down. Nothing breaks it but making something.
gene_keys.gift:
Lean into what shakes you and the whole thing turns. A shock met with harshness, whether you run from it or set your jaw and try to fix it, is a coat pulled tighter in a cold wind; met with softness, the way the sun gets the coat off, it opens. In one of the old fighting arts, when the blow comes you lean into it rather than against it, and the other person flies across the room without your quite knowing how. Go into the agitation like that, make room around it, listen to it, and the charge that rattled you becomes the charge to move.

What it moves you onto is your own path, the one nobody has walked, with no net under it. Every teacher is at best a mirror, and none can tell you where your feet go. You stop competing with people and start using them as mirrors of your own best; your difference from them turns from a flaw into your genius. Your deepest fear meets you on this road, and it does not stop you. Go first. Life supports the one who does, and it will shock you with good fortune.
gene_keys.siddhi:
Awake or asleep: there are two states, and every ladder somebody has drawn between them was drawn by a sleeper grading their own dreams. Waking comes once, without cause, and stays. Nothing you practise brings it. It has happened to kind people and to cruel ones. It comes to someone so completely themselves that it has no choice, and you cannot work at being yourself. It is not a leap you take. The leap takes you.

After it there is nothing left in you for a shock to land on, because there is no separate one there to be struck. What is left is a vessel that knows only how to give, with nothing in the way, and the giving is love, though not always the warm kind. Even now your presence stirs the room. The sound that frightened you at the bottom is, at the top, the sound of you giving.
gene_keys.programming_partner: Every thunderclap needs air soft enough to move through, which is UL 57, The Gentle Wind, the soft intuitive penetration that is this code's exact counterweight. Thunder is the sudden shock, the wind is the soft yielding that meets it, and the teaching is that you cannot survive your own thunder without that softness. To pass through a real shock a person has to become pliant, not braced. Loud and quiet, bolt and breeze, holding each other up.

human_design.gate: Gate 51 is the pressure to come through a shock changed, and what it drives you to do is go first into the unknown. It is the door the unexpected uses, the sudden turn or the loss, arriving in your life more often than in most. The pressure is not to avoid it but to be the one who takes the hit and stands up stronger. People built around this have a nerve for the edge, a pull toward whatever nobody has tried, and other people feel it as a charge in the room. The cost, from outside, is a life that looks volatile, a person who seems to court the upheaval they say they suffer, and who can shock others just for the effect. Some of that is true. The pressure has to go somewhere, and shocking people without regard for what it does to them is this drive spent badly. People who carry this all their lives learn to keep their faith through the turn, to use the disruption rather than resent it, and to tell a shock that wakes someone from one that only jolts them.
human_design.centre:
The place this pressure comes from is a small triangle over the heart, the Will centre, the smallest of the nine places and one of the four that make energy. It holds worth, the capacity to act, the part of you that says I can and then does. It is a motor built for bursts: it works to rest, and pushed on without the rest it burns out, so the nerve to leap draws on a reserve that has to fill again.

In about four people in ten this centre is switched on: they say what they will do and then do it, they keep a promise, they prove themselves for the pleasure of it. For someone like that, what starves them is a push with no rest behind it, or a leap made to prove something rather than because it was theirs. In the other six it is not, so they take in the worth of whoever is near them and feel it as their own. Beside someone sure of themselves they can do anything, and when that person leaves the capacity goes too. Left with the question of their own worth, they may spend a life proving it and burn themselves down. What is theirs, once the proving stops, is a fine sense of what is worth anything, and a worth that was never the earned kind: an orchid is worth no more than a dandelion.
human_design.channel: A shock on its own means nothing yet; it can wake you or only rattle you. Its other half is Gate 25, in the centre of the chest, the part of you that loves life without choosing anyone. Together they make the Channel of Initiation, the one path off the will whose force is not the wish to do. Through it a blow to your world becomes an initiation, never planned, gone through alone, and you land somewhere with more room. Whether the other half is yours or someone's near you, the shock becomes a door where the two meet.

tarot.ring_role: Within the Ring of Humanity, this code is the moment of initiation, the shock that wakes. Its siblings, UL 10, 17, 21, 25, and 38, carry the rest of what it means to be human: the way you walk through the world, the views you follow, the control that bites through, the innocent heart, and the fighter for what matters. Bound by a single amino acid, they are the chemistry of the human spirit finding its own way.
tarot.tarot_resonance: Both trigrams here are thunder, so the two Tarot axes fold into one. The codon ring gives the Chariot, the one who masters the wild forces and steers them forward by sheer will. The doubled thunder gives the Tower and Judgement, the shock that breaks the structure open and the trumpet that calls the new life up. Together they say one thing: the shattering is a waking, and the will can take the reins and drive it home.

body.physiology:
This energy is given to the gallbladder, and the reason is decision. It is a small bag under the right of your liver, and it makes nothing. What your liver makes flows into it between meals and waits, while the water is drawn out of it, until it is five to ten times as strong. Then fat from a meal reaches your gut, the gut sends word, and the whole bag squeezes, emptied within the hour without deliberating, then still until the next. That is the shape of this energy in you: a long holding, a charge that grows the longer it is kept, one act that empties it. The gall you need to do a thing is named for it.

Its tip comes to your belly wall under the right ribs, where the outer edge of the flat belly muscle meets the bone. A finger finds the notch; the gallbladder itself cannot be felt. Rest your hand there and you are resting it on the part of you that will not be hurried, nor stopped once it starts.
body.amino_acid:
The nerve to go first has a substance in you, and the substance is arginine. Your body makes it for itself, it is built into every protein you are made of, and it comes in with eggs, or with a handful of seeds. Leaving the crowd for the wild country of your own heart is a road every human spirit walks at some point, and the road has a chemistry, this one, the same in you as in everyone who ever set out. In you it is the substance of the step off the known path.

The first place it was ever found was a seedling, as a salt of silver, and what is in you is still named for silver. What wakes one person in the end wakes everyone, family by family, and the chemistry of that waking is already in you, shared with your kin.

relations.unity_line: Read alongside UL 52, this is the whole motion of the shock and the stillness, the thunder that wakes and the mountain that lets it pass.

pair.teaching: Together with The Still Mountain, these two are the deck's pair of arrest and arousal. One is the thunder that breaks a life open, the other is the mountain that sits unmoved while the storm passes over it. Movement and stillness are the same teaching seen from two ends, and a person needs both, the nerve to be shaken and the ground to not be carried off.

inverse.teaching: Turn this hexagram upside down and the thunder becomes the mountain. The same lines that arouse, read from the other end, hold perfectly still. What looks like a life cracked open by shock is, flipped over, a life learning where to stop and stay. The shake and the stillness are one structure seen from opposite sides.

sky.teaching: the cardinal water of the home and the shell, the soft inner life the shock breaks open, the one who must learn to be cracked without being destroyed.

immortals.teaching: Both trigrams are the same thunder, so a single figure stands above and below: Cao Guo Jiu, who walked away from the inherited court and its borrowed power. Doubled here, he teaches that the one who can survive the great shock is the one who has already let go of the false security of rank and name, who has nothing left that the thunder can take.

hebrew_letter.teaching: the enclosure, the field marked off and held, the boundary that gives the wild charge something to drive within. The path it walks is the one the Chariot rides, the disciplined vessel that carries the force forward.

cards.essence: This energy is coming to rest. Everything that moves has to stop somewhere. In you this is the part that knows where: the weight that settles at the end of a cycle and holds there until the next one is ready. Carried well it is not the absence of movement. The outside holds still so that the inside can move.

glance.reading:
This energy is coming to rest. Everything that moves has to stop somewhere. In you this is the part that knows where: the weight that settles at the end of a cycle and holds there until the next one is ready. Carried well it is not the absence of movement. The outside holds still so that the inside can move.

The long view is this energy breathed low. You take your time as a matter of course, in seasons rather than minutes, and waiting costs you nothing. Your breath reaches all the way down, and from there nothing can hurry you. People slow near you without being told, and what looked urgent sorts itself into an order you can see. What you begin from fear carries the fear into everything that grows from it, so you do not begin until the fear has gone. Once you are calm, the way forward is usually plain.

The way is down. Let the weight fall through the seat and the heels until the breath follows it to the floor of you. There will be stretches when you feel stuck, unable to get off the ground, and stuck is a feeling before it is a fact: the breath has stopped short of the base, in a rhythm you have not yet agreed to. Nothing is lost in the waiting.

iching.trigram_combination: Mountain over Mountain: one peak standing on another, and nothing between them moves. The traditional character is an eye held on the one thing close in front of it, the look of someone who has stopped. Its scene is someone keeping the back still, walking their own courtyard and seeing nobody in it, at rest in the place where rest belongs.
iching.reading:
Whatever you are asking about has gone as far as it goes, and this is the stop at the end of it. A cycle has closed, and before the next one opens there is a pause to see where you are. The eyes reach for what they see and the hands for what they can hold; the back reaches for nothing. All it has to do is stand straight and carry you. Rest your attention there and the reaching lets go of you. Then you can walk through your own house with people in every room and not be pulled at by any of them. This is not the stillness of someone who has left the world. You are among people, still alone, doing what is right whether anyone is watching or not.

What it asks is that you stop in the place where stopping belongs. Stop in its season, move in its season, and nothing is missed. When you are lost, do not wander; stay where you are, and a path clears. The one who has stopped can see what is coming, which the one still moving cannot. The danger is a stop held with the jaw, in anger or in pride, and that is not stillness but obstinacy wearing its clothes.

In the body this energy is the back. Notice where you are holding yourself now. Let the back stand straight, let the weight go down through it, and keep still there, low, so that nothing above it has to hold on.
judgement_lines: Keep still at the back, and the body drops out of mind.
Walk your own courtyard and see no one there.
No fault.
Stop when it is the season for stopping, move when it is the season for moving, and the way stays bright.
image_lines: Mountains stand joined, one beside the other.
Thought keeps to the place it stands in and does not go out past it.

upper_trigram.name: Mountain (Ken)
upper_trigram.nature: Limit, frontier, stillness. Solid, steady, unshakable. The youngest son.

lower_trigram.name: Mountain (Ken)
lower_trigram.nature: Limit, frontier, stillness. Solid, steady, unshakable. The youngest son.

lines.image: toes held still before the first step.
lines.reading: Stopped at the toes, before the first step, and nothing has gone wrong yet. This is the easiest stop there is, made before there is anything to undo. You are soft here and could be led, so the stop needs holding, not once but every day it is asked of you. Stop at the outset, and keep to it.

lines.image: the calves held still, the heart not glad.
lines.reading: Stopped at the calves, while the one you follow walks on out of reach. The calves do not decide; they go where the feet go. Yours are halted by someone who will not turn back to listen, so you are still without having chosen it and the heart is sour. A stop you did not choose is not peace. Do not call being left behind a stillness.

lines.image: the waist locked, the spine wrenched, the heart smoking.
lines.reading: Stopped at the waist, the one place in you built to bend, and the spine locks. The top of you and the bottom no longer speak. What could not go down goes up into the chest, where it smoulders as the wish to win and be done. This is strength forcing a stop it does not mean. Unclench, and let the stop go lower than the waist.

lines.image: the trunk held still, the self governed.
lines.reading: Stopped at the trunk, the whole middle of you at rest, and there is no fault in it. You keep your own house: you answer for what is yours and push none of it onto anyone else. Most wrong turns begin in the body, in the reach or the flinch, and stopped there they never become anything. Govern yourself, and leave the judging of others alone.

lines.image: the jaws at rest, the words in order.
lines.reading: Stopped at the jaw, so the mouth no longer opens at random. What you say now has an order to it, weighed before it leaves you, and what you regretted saying dissolves. The hardest silence is the one about what matters most to you, and it is the one that makes you. Speak when the words have found their order, and not before.

lines.image: stillness kept generously, through to the end.
lines.reading: Stopped all the way through, inside and outside one rest, with nothing being held down. The wish for a quick finish has gone; what is left is generous and thorough. Steady as the peak and lasting as the ground, you complete what was begun. Keep still like this to the end, and it brings good fortune.

gene_keys.shadow:
The pressure you live under was not made by you. It is in the room before you walk in, put there by everyone alive, and in a city you are never out of it, not even alone in your own bed. The first thing it does is lift the breath. Somewhere in growing up the breath left your belly for the top of your chest, and from there the whole day runs on short supply. Time changes shape with it: it stops being something you stand in and becomes something you are behind on, too fast or too slow, never yours.

The usual move is to hand the trouble to the mind, and the mind sets off to fix it. The running is the pressure, so every plan to end it feeds it. Nobody enjoys the rush; most of us are used to it, which is close to wanting it. The body sounds an alarm when your rhythm falls out of step with the one around you, and most people live with it ringing until it sounds like silence. The alarm is not the enemy. It asks one thing: stop, breathe low, come back down to the base of yourself.
gene_keys.repressive: One kind of person goes down under it. The pressure lands and they fold. A heavy jammed feeling settles into the body and stays, until getting off the ground seems impossible. They read it as a wall. The way out is to be of use to someone else.
gene_keys.reactive: The other kind runs. They cannot sit down, so they fill every hour to stay ahead of the quiet that would show them how shallow the breath has gone, and their frustration lands on whoever is nearest. It passes for drive. What it burns is them, until they turn and look at the fear underneath.
gene_keys.gift:
Everything alive has its own speed, and you know this in your body before you know it in your head. A yew seed and a sunflower seed are much the same size. The sunflower is full grown by the end of summer; the yew takes ten years to reach that height, then lives for thousands. The large things begin slowly, and hurrying either one disturbs the ground it was sown in.

You cannot be stuck while you are still in touch with what you meant. You can only be paused, and the pause is where the growing happens, out of sight, the way buds form before anything shows. What you began with is the seed, and it already holds everything the thing will need, even what draws the right people at the right time. Your work is not to interfere out of fear. Someone who lives like this is an anchor: not a weight that stops the boat, but what lets it rest and find where it is. Once you are calm the way forward is plain, and one question paces the rest. How can you be of the greatest use?
gene_keys.siddhi:
Push any movement to either end and you arrive at the same place. Slowed to nothing, it stops; quickened past all measure, it runs together, which is also a stop. Stillness waits at both ends, and it is not empty but full, more alive than what it replaced. Your body goes on being rebuilt every hour, and underneath the building nothing moves at all.

A thought arrives with a gap before the next. A feeling rises so slowly you could reach out and turn it over before it breaks the surface. Then it spreads through you like a coin dropped in a pond, and dissolves back into the quiet it came from. Nothing in you wants back into the drama; you watch it from a little way off. Near someone this still, other people's thinking goes quiet on its own and time seems to widen. Whatever moves from here moves only to touch the same stillness in someone else.
gene_keys.programming_partner: Opposite this code the Gene Keys place UL 58, Rhythm of Life, and the pairing is the one that wears the body down or sets it free. The partner's low face is dissatisfaction, the itch that nothing is quite right; this one's is the sense that there is never enough time, and the two run together in most lives as the deepest pattern under bad health. Lifted, they rise together. Stopping and feeling alive need each other: the lake needs the mountain to stop long enough to feel anything, and the mountain needs the lake so the stop has a pulse in it. At the very top, stillness and bliss turn out to be one shape seen from its two ends, the way a whirlpool draws in and a spring pours out.

human_design.gate:
Low in you there is a pressure that has not been told where to go. Gate 52 is the door it comes through: a charge held at the base, large enough to drive a whole life, waiting for its aim. The bow is drawn and the arrow has no target yet. Meanwhile the whole field opens at once, the shape of what needs to happen and the order it needs to happen in. The pull is either to freeze in front of so much or to spend the charge on whatever is nearest. When the aim is found you can sit on one thing for hours while the room forgets you are in it, and the hard part is stopping.

From outside this is called slowness, or being lost in your own world, and when you are deep in something it can look like not caring. What is being watched is someone who will not fire until the aim is true, and then does not stop. People who carry this all their lives learn that the wait before the aim is part of the work, and that the charge is still there when the aim comes.
human_design.centre:
The base of the trunk is where this pressure sits, the Root Centre, the part of you that presses you to move. It is a motor that pulses rather than runs. On, you could move a mountain; off, you cannot make yourself do what you know you did yesterday. Living with it means living at the mercy of that timing. When the pulse is on and nothing has been chosen, the charge backs up. You feel rattled, agitated for no reason you could name, and the urge is to force it down any channel at all to be rid of the pressure.

In about six people in ten this centre is switched on, and the pressure is theirs whoever they are with. For someone like that, pressure is a familiar weight, and the work is to wait through the off pulse without deciding something is wrong with them. In the other four it is not, so the pressure is borrowed from whoever is nearest, made louder, then let go when they leave. For someone like that every room is a kitchen that needs cleaning, and the cleaning never ends because the pressure was never theirs. The other move is to shut down under it and do nothing. The same person, when the pressure is clear, can do in a day what takes others a week, and grows wise about which pressures are worth answering at all.
human_design.channel: A pressure with no aim needs the part of you that picks one thing. Its other half is Gate 9, low in the belly, the narrowing that says yes or no in the gut before any reason arrives and stays on one detail. Together they make the Channel of Concentration: the pulse from the base turned into patient focus, the kind that pulls whoever is near into the same track. Between the two there is a wait nobody can shorten. Whether the other half sits in you or in someone near you, the stillness holds until the belly has chosen.

tarot.ring_role: Six codes share this ring, and every one of them is a pressure. Magnetism pulls, dynamism provokes, expansion pushes out, aspiration climbs, vitality burns, and this code is the only member holding all of that in check. Its kin are UL 15, 39, 53, 54 and 58, and without this one among them the family would spend itself in a season. Restraint is what lets the seeking last long enough to find anything. It is the torque the whole ring turns on, the pause in which the searching finally hears something back.
tarot.tarot_resonance: The one who kept still at the back, walking the courtyard and seeing no one, is the Hermit on his peak, and here every road leads to him. The ring gives the Hermit. The trigram gives the Hermit, and gives him twice, because both halves of this hexagram are Mountain. There is no second face to argue with. One figure alone at the summit has stopped climbing and holds the lantern low, and the light is for whoever is still coming up.

body.physiology:
This energy lives at the floor of your body, in the perineum, and the reason is the breath. The perineum is the small floor of muscle between your legs. Each breath you take arises from it and returns to it; nothing in you is lower. At the other end of your spine is the soft spot on the crown of your head, and the two hold the spine between them. When the breath reaches the floor, you are at rest, and everything above it settles. When it stops short, high in the chest, you are already hurrying.

Sit down and let your weight settle. It rests on two bones, one under each side, with the perineum between them: you sit on either side of it, never on it. Breathe in and it gives a little, with the belly. Breathe out and it lifts. It has moved with every breath since your first. Let the breath go all the way down to it, and you are resting on the part of you that stops.
body.amino_acid:
There is more life in you than you can spend, pressing to get out. That pressure has a substance in you, and the substance is serine. It is one of the twenty pieces you are built from, in nearly every protein in you. When one of the proteins in you is to be stopped, or started again, a small mark is set on it, and four times in five the mark lands on a serine. Of the pressures in you this is the one that makes the others last.

Under fear your body makes the rush that runs you, and while it lasts there is no rest in you. You can get so used to it that you go looking for it. At the far end your body makes something else, a chemistry that quiets thought, so the stillness is in your body before it is in your mind.

relations.unity_line: Read with UL 51, the mountain that holds and the thunder that breaks it open are one pulse, caught at its two ends.

pair.teaching: Read from the other end, the peak is a shock. Thunder rises up out of the ground; the mountain brings things to rest; and the old sequence sets them side by side because you never get one without the other. A jolt is what ends a stillness held too long, and stillness is what the body goes looking for the moment the jolt has passed. Unshakable Arrival is the instant the quiet breaks. This is the quiet it breaks, and the quiet that comes back after.
